name: SAML Assertion/Response Signature Validation Disabled
attack_scenario: With signatures not enforced, an attacker replays or hand-crafts a SAML response (or wraps an extra unsigned assertion around a signed one) asserting subject=admin; the SP consumes the attacker-chosen NameID and authenticates them as any user, a full auth bypass.
negative_test_hint: forge an unsigned SAML response asserting NameID = "attacker-admin@evil.example.com" and assert the service provider rejects it and establishes no session

exemplar.explanation: CVE-2020-5407 (spring-security-saml2 signature wrapping) plus JPCERT/OpenSAML guidance: SAML security assumes every assertion/response is signed and the SP validates it against a trusted IdP cert. Turning wantAssertionsSigned/signatureRequired/setValidateSignature off lets an attacker replay or hand-craft a response asserting any identity, a full authentication bypass. Requiring signatures makes the SP reject anything the IdP did not actually sign.
